ctx.x: then I played with Tiny about six months in the club there. And Billie Holiday was singing in the club. We backed her, in fact. And the other act in there was Art Tatum. That's -- those were the two acts in that club. That was also the Yacht Club on 52nd, Club. It was right across the street from the Onyx Club. Yeah.

And I had a ball playing for her. I couldn't get out of the room because Art Tatum was coming on after her, you know. I just went to the john and that was about it, man, and I came back on. Yeah, it was a lot of fun. And Tiny had a good little band. John Hardee -- I don't know if you ever knew him -- a tenor man was playing tenor, myself, and Curly Russell was on bass, and Marlowe Morris was on piano, and the drummer Harold was West -- Eddie West -- not Harold West -- Eddie West, I think, was the drummer from…

But we backed her, you know. And Tiny had the gig. It was Tiny's gig. You know, in those days it didn't matter who the leader was. Whoever got the gig, he was the leader, man. You know, that was it, you know. And he had the gig. And he might leave right out of there and another guy get a gig, and Tiny be playing the guy's band -- one of the guys who was in that band. That's how things always worked back there then, you know.
